reason: 'Panicled' says the flowers or inflorescence are arranged as a panicle. A rule that only says a panicle is present loses that.
Bulbiform means bulb-shaped, and 'bulblike' is a synonym of bulbous.
Knobbed means bearing knobs, which is knobbled. Head-shaped (capitate) is a different word.
'Crisp' can mean crisped (a curled margin) on leaves and petals. On other parts it can mean a brittle texture.
Sarmentose means bearing long, slender, trailing or whip-like shoots. That is not the same as climbing, and it loses the runner or trailing sense.
Stunted means dwarfed in growth, and the rule already limits it to whole-plant parts.
Nectariferous means nectar-bearing, so a nectary is present.
Ecarunculate means without a caruncle, so the caruncle is absent.
'Not decurrent' is the negation of decurrent.
Well-defined means distinct or sharply delimited, not conspicuous. The two can differ.
Pronounced means prominent.
Hippocrepiform means horseshoe-shaped, which is a synonym of U-shaped.
'Equal in length' is a case of equal size for a set of like parts.
Strophiolate means bearing a strophiole.
Brush-like means brush-like shape.
Embedded means sunk in or enclosed by another tissue, such as seeds in pulp or glands in the surface. That is a position, not the sunken shape of a surface.
Disk-like is a listed synonym of discoid.
In floras 'strict' means stiffly erect and straight.
Spikelike means spike-like. I could not read the term's definition, because the lookup output was truncated.
Foliate means bearing leaves, which matches the definition of leafy.
Needle-like is a synonym of subulate in the lexicon.
Hairlike means thread-like, which is filiform.
Invisible means cannot be seen at all. Inconspicuous only means hard to see, so the rule loses the absolute sense.
Superposed means placed one above another, which is stacked.
Ribbon-like means strap-shaped.
Appressed-puberulous means fine short hairs lying flat, which is close to strigulose. I could not read the term's definition, because the lookup output was truncated.
Cobwebby means arachnose.
A thyrse is a panicle whose side branches are cymose, which is what cymose-paniculate describes.
Gland-like means resembling a gland, but it is not a gland. Glandular means bearing glands.
Asperulous means minutely rough, which falls under scabrous.
Didymous means twin, as in two-lobed anthers or fruits. Bilobed is an acceptable approximation.
Veiny means conspicuously veined. The rule says only that veins are present and loses the conspicuousness. The target is also the vascular bundle, not the leaf vein.
'Level' is vague. It can mean even or flat, or level with a surface, and flush is not the general sense.
Hoary means covered with fine greyish-white hairs, which is canescent.
Clawless means not clawed.
Tetragonous means four-angled, which is quadrangular.
Russet means reddish brown.
Declinate means bent or curved downward. I could not check this against the term's definition.
Bumpy means having irregular lumps, which is knobbled.
Beardless means not bearded.
Knotty means lumpy or knobby. It is a loose match to knobbled.
Imbricated is the same as imbricate.
Clambering means climbing or scrambling. It is a loose match to climbing.
Obdeltoid means obtriangular.
Ribless means not ribbed.
Thin-textured means thin, with decreased thickness.
Laminate is ambiguous. It can mean layered or flattened, so it does not reliably mean that a lamina is present.
Coalescent means fused together, which is connate.
Tetrahedral means a four-faced solid with triangular faces. Pyramidal loses the four-face and triangular-face detail.
Farinaceous means mealy.
